Ready for a challenge?
Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.
Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.
About this role
JET's Security Architecture & Engineering function is responsible for making data protection a built-in property of how we design and operate our platforms, not an afterthought. As Data Security Specialist, you'll be responsible for engineering the controls that safeguard JET's most sensitive structured and unstructured data across cloud-native and enterprise environments. You'll translate architectural data security standards into working, scalable implementations  from DLP platforms to encryption pipelines, and embed Privacy and Security by Design into engineering delivery.
You'll work at the intersection of data security engineering and automation, engineering to turn continuous insights like data security findings into automated engineering guardrails. Utilising CI/CD pipelines, and LLM-driven automation, your vision will enhance our automated data defense, your execution will deliver continuous compliance and risk reduction, and your approach will care deeply about creating frictionless security workflows that enable development teams to innovate safely. Together with engineering, IT, and business stakeholders, you'll drive a culture where security isn't a hurdle, it's a competitive advantage that helps us win together.
These are some of the key components to the position:
• Oversee the deployment and daily management of Enterprise DLP and encryption solutions across network, cloud, endpoint, and AI environments to protect data at rest, in transit, and in use.
• Manage automated data discovery pipelines to ensure sensitive information is accurately mapped and protected, extending these controls to AI-integrated environments (e.g., training datasets, model inputs, and inference logs).
• Collaborate with the Security Architecture team to embed data protection controls, cryptography, and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) baselines directly into CI/CD developer workflows.
• Translate written data security and compliance policies into executable "Policy-as-Code" (e.g., OPA) and manage the deployment of automated guardrails and remediation scripts across cloud environments.
• Streamline engineering workflows by building API integrations between security scanners and ticketing systems, and utilize intelligent automation to parse, prioritize, and tune data security alerts (reducing false positives).
• Guide engineering teams by providing automated feedback loops, clear technical documentation, and developer-friendly data protection tools that prevent leaks before deployment.
What will you bring to the team?
• Proven experience implementing and managing data security controls in cloud-native or enterprise environments, spanning DSPM platforms (e.g., Wiz), Enterprise DLP, cryptography, and data classification programs.
• Strong automation and scripting skills (Python & Bash/Shell). You're comfortable translating security goals into working code, remediation scripts, and infrastructure-as-code.
• Strong track record of translating governance policies and security alerts into automated remediation workflows and CI/CD security gates, ensuring robust protection without disrupting engineering velocity.
• Practical understanding of AI/ML data security risks (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, prompt injection, and training data exposure), coupled with experience using AI tools to automate security tasks like alert triaging and data classification.
• A highly collaborative approach with the ability to build trusted partnerships across DevOps, Software Engineering, IT, and Privacy teams, acting as an enabler rather than a blocker.
• Strong ability to evaluate complex data flows and translate dense security findings into clear, actionable code comments, documentation, and developer-friendly alerts.
• A solid understanding of data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR) and a strong ethical foundation, setting the standard for the secure handling of highly sensitive structured and unstructured data.
At JET, this is how we play
Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.
Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.
At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.
Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.
Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging
No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.
What else are we delivering?
Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET journeys.

The Large-Scale Fisheries Project Director leads The Nature Conservancy's efforts to work with governments and other stakeholders to design, implement, and scale electronic monitoring (EM) programs that improve fisheries management, transparency, and accountability across industrial fisheries operating in Africa and Europe. The Project Director serves as a principal representative for TNC's fisheries transparency initiatives, providing strategic, technical, and partnership leadership to advance the adoption of effective EM strategies and the use of fisheries data to support sustainable management decisions.
The location for this position is flexible within countries in Europe and Africa where The Nature Conservancy is a registered NGO and has an established office in Europe (these include Croatia, Belgium, Germany, and the UK) and in Africa (these include Angola, Gabon, Kenya, South Africa, Tanzania, and Zambia).
Essential Functions:
The Project Director establishes TNC as a trusted partner in the design and implementation of electronic monitoring programs. They build strategic partnerships with government agencies, industry stakeholders, regional fisheries management organizations, technology providers, and civil society organizations to strengthen fisheries monitoring and management systems.
The Project Director provides technical support for the design, implementation, evaluation, and scaling of EM programs, including policy frameworks, operational models, governance arrangements, financing approaches, and implementation roadmaps. They work collaboratively with stakeholders to identify barriers, develop practical solutions, and integrate EM data into fisheries management, compliance, and decision-making processes.
The Director develops and manages multi-stakeholder collaborations, builds technical and institutional capacity, negotiates complex solutions, and facilitates policy dialogue to advance effective and sustainable EM programs. They represent TNC in national, regional, and international forums and communicate best practices, lessons learned, and innovative approaches that accelerate fisheries transparency and accountability
We’re Looking for You:
If you’re looking for a career where you can find meaning and purpose, come join our Large Scales Fisheries program as a key Project Director to support biodiversity and sustainable fisheries. Not only will you fulfill conservation objectives across the oceans but you will also support TNC's ambitious global goals for positive outcomes for both nature and people.
We’re looking for a passionate, dedicated person to lead our LSF projects across Africa and Europe. Systems Leadership, creativity, and the ability to influence without authority are key in this role. Come join TNC and apply today!

• BA/BS degree and 5 years’ experience in conservation practice or equivalent combination of education and experience.
• Experience managing complex or multiple projects, including staffing, workloads and finances under deadlines.
• Supervisory experience, including motivating, leading, setting objectives and managing performance.
• Experience in partnership development with non-profit partners, community groups and/or   government agencies
• Experience negotiating.

• Knowledge of current trends, best practices, and emerging issues related to electronic monitoring, fisheries transparency, sustainable seafood, and industrial fisheries management.
• Strong strategic thinking, analytical, negotiation, and problem-solving skills.
• Experience working in a highly matrixed, decentralized, and collaborative organization.
• Excellent written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
• Proficiency in French or Swahili is preferred.
• Politically savvy, with demonstrated ability to influence decision-makers and build consensus among diverse stakeholders.

This position may be based in European and African countries where TNC has an established entity, taking into consideration legal restrictions, such as non-national ratios and immigration processing times. Your geographic location will be confirmed during the recruitment and used to determine your actual pay range. Additionally, for all applicants, actual pay will fall within a range based on a variety of factors including, for example, the candidate’s qualifications, specific skills, and experience.

The Nature Conservancy’s mission is to protect the lands and waters upon which all life depends. As a science-based organization, we create innovative, on-the-ground solutions to our world’s toughest challenges so that we can create a world in which people and nature thrive. We’re rooted in our mission and guided by our values, which include respect for all people, communities, and cultures. Whether it’s career development, flexible schedules, or a rewarding mission, there’s many reasons to love life inside TNC. Want a better insight to TNC? Check out our TNC Talent playlist on YouTube   to hear stories from staff or visit  Glassdoor.
One goal is to cultivate an inclusive work environment so that all our colleagues around the globe feel a sense of belonging and that their unique contributions to our mission are valued. In addition to the requirements in our job postings, we recognize that people come with talent and experiences outside of a job and consider each applicant’s unique experience. Please apply – we’d love to hear from you. To quote a popular saying at TNC, “you’ll join for the mission, and stay for the people.”
What We Bring:
Since 1951, TNC has been doing work you can believe in. Through grassroots action, we have grown from a small non-profit into one of the most effective and wide-reaching environmental organizations in the world. Thanks to more than 1 million members, over 400 scientists, and the dedicated efforts of our diverse staff and partners, we impact conservation around the world!

Monitor construction progress through detailed measurement and evaluation of installed quantities against approved plans and baseline estimates

Develop and maintain forecasting models, including estimate loading and cost projections aligned with project schedules and delivery milestones
•
Perform cost-benefit analysis, value engineering assessments, and feasibility studies to optimise labour, materials, and execution strategies

Analyse variances between planned and actual quantities and provide insights to support corrective actions and commercial decisions

Contribute to project controls reporting by integrating quantity, cost, and progress data into standard reporting deliverables

Interpret internal and external project issues, applying technical expertise to develop practical solutions and best practices

Coordinate with cross-functional stakeholders including engineering, planning, and commercial teams to ensure data consistency and alignment

Support compliance with company policies, procedures, and project governance frameworks in all quantity surveying activities

Previous experience in quantity surveying within construction, EPC, or infrastructure projects

Proven experience with quantity tracking, measurement, and progress reporting on large-scale projects
•
Experience developing forecasts, cost estimates, and project controls reporting

Experience interpreting and working from Issued for Construction (IFC) drawings
•
Experience in value engineering and cost analysis within project delivery environments
Desirable
•
Experience working within integrated project controls environments
•
Knowledge of earned value management and cost control methodologies
•
Experience mentoring or leading junior quantity surveying staff
•
Experience working on multi-discipline or complex capital projects
Technical Skills/Knowledge
•
Quantity tracking and installed quantity measurement on construction projects
•
Material Take-Off (MTO) development and updating from IFC drawings
•
Cost forecasting and estimate loading within project controls environments
•
Progress measurement methodologies (e.g. earned value, quantity-based tracking)
•
Cost benefit analysis and commercial performance evaluation
•
Value engineering and feasibility study execution across labour, materials, and scope

Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Engineering, or related discipline

Chartered status (RICS or equivalent professional body)

• Experience supporting, administering or implementing an operational or work management system.

csl.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/csl_external/j.description_excerpt:
Senior Clinical Statistical Programmer (Portfolio Development / Biometrics / Programming)
The Role
CSL is looking for a Senior Programmer to take technical ownership of one or two clinical trials from first line of code to final submission package. This is a hands-on statistical programming role with real authority attached to it: you'll be the person a study team turns to when the data needs to hold up under regulatory scrutiny, and the person who decides how a dataset gets built, not just who builds it. You'll work alongside statisticians, data managers, medical writers and regulatory colleagues as a peer, not a downstream resource — reading protocols and SAPs early enough to shape how a study's analysis gets structured, then seeing that structure through to submission-ready SDTM and ADaM datasets, TFLs, and supporting documentation.
Hybrid Based (3 days a week onsite) in Maidenhead
Why It Matters
Clinical data is only as useful as the programming behind it is trustworthy. Every regulatory decision downstream — every safety signal caught or missed, every submission accepted or queried — traces back to whether the datasets and outputs were built right the first time. This role sits at that pressure point. You're not just executing specifications; you're often the one writing them, catching the ambiguity in a protocol before it becomes a data problem three months later, and making the judgment calls that keep a study's analysis both scientifically sound and audit-ready.
What You'll Be Responsible For
You'll lead end-to-end programming for your assigned studies — in-house or outsourced — spanning the full clinical development lifecycle from study setup through analysis, reporting, and regulatory submission. That means building and validating datasets and outputs yourself where the work is done internally, and holding CRO-delivered work to the same bar where it isn't. You'll also be a technical reference point for less experienced programmers, and a contributor to how the wider programming function does its work.
·         Serve as lead programmer for one or two clinical trials, interpreting protocols, SAPs, data management plans, and CRF specifications to drive study setup and analysis
·         Design and validate SDTM and ADaM datasets, tables, figures, and listings, in partnership with study statisticians
·         Review and take ownership of CRO-produced deliverables, ensuring submission-ready quality before they go further
·         Lead specification and delivery of integrated analyses (e.g. ISS/ISE) and associated outputs when not handled by a CRO
·         Mentor other programmers on internal processes and standards, and contribute to departmental tools and process improvements
·         Take on ad hoc analytical work — regulatory query responses, exploratory analyses, publication support — as studies require it
Experience Required
·         Experience of programming in pharmaceutical, biotech, CRO, or clinical research settings
·         Strong SAS proficiency (Base/Macro/Stat/Graph); familiarity with R or other languages is a plus
·         Working knowledge of current CDISC standards — CDASH, SDTM, ADaM, define.xml
·         Track record of producing and validating submission-ready TFLs and datasets, including ad hoc analytical requests
·         Experience supporting regulatory submissions (FDA required; PMDA, NMPA, or EMA experience a plus)
·         Comfort working with external vendors and CRO-managed data
·         BSc in Computer Science, Mathematics, Statistics or a related field — equivalent experience and certifications will also be considered
About CSL Seqirus
CSL Seqirus is part of CSL. As one of the largest influenza vaccine providers in the world, CSL Seqirus is a major contributor to the prevention of influenza globally and a transcontinental partner in pandemic preparedness. With state-of-the-art production facilities in the U.S., the U.K. and Australia, CSL Seqirus utilizes egg, cell and adjuvant technologies to offer a broad portfolio of differentiated influenza vaccines in more than 20 countries around the world.
To learn more about CSL, CSL Behring, CSL Seqirus and CSL Vifor visit https://www.csl.com/ and CSL Plasma at https://www.cslplasma.com/.
Our Benefits

You Belong at CSL
At CSL, Inclusion and Belonging is at the core of our mission and who we are. It fuels our innovation day in and day out. By celebrating our differences and creating a culture of curiosity and empathy, we are able to better understand and connect with our patients and donors, foster strong relationships with our stakeholders, and sustain a diverse workforce that will move our company and industry into the future.

Personal Lines Insurance Apprenticeship Programme
Build Relationships, Solve Problems and Help People Protect What Matters Most
Ready to earn, learn and launch your career? This is more than your first job. You’ll gain real experience, work towards a recognised Level 3 insurance qualification and build skills that will shape your future.
Our Personal Lines division operates across more than 100 high street branches and offices, supporting individuals and families protect the things that matter most. From home, car, private medical and critical illness cover, we deliver specialist personal insurance solutions and find the best possible cover, price and terms for our clients.
Join our supportive and high-performing Sales team and help connect clients with the insurance solutions they need. You'll gain hands-on experience in sales, learn how to build strong client relationships, and develop the skills needed to win new business in a fast-paced, target-driven environment.
You’ll join Howden on a permanent role and complete an 18-month development programme designed to develop your technical knowledge, professional skills and confidence to kick start your career.
What you’ll be doing?
You will begin with a structured induction before joining our Personal Lines team, where you will work alongside experienced colleagues and gradually take on more responsibility.
During the programme, you'll:
• Learn the foundations of insurance, customer service and sales through hands-on experience and structured training.
• Support colleagues in finding suitable insurance solutions for new and existing clients.
• Play an active role in achieving sales goals by securing new business opportunities and supporting client renewals.
• Develop your written communication skills by preparing professional client correspondence.
• Build confidence speaking with clients and insurers, helping to answer queries and gather information, both via email and during phone calls.
• Learn how to build long-term relationships and provide excellent customer service.
• Support with maintaining accurate and up-to-date client records.
• Learn how amendments to insurance policies are managed as well as the policy renewals process.
Who are we looking for?
No insurance experience is needed; we’ll teach you everything you need to know!

• Confident communicating with a wide range of people, including over the phone.

• Curious and motivated to learn, with a genuine interest in developing your knowledge and skills.
• Energised by targets and committed to delivering results, even when situations become challenging.
• Someone who enjoys building positive relationships and working with others.
• Able to express your ideas clearly, both verbally and in writing.
• Comfortable working with numbers and handling basic numerical information accurately.
• Organised, dependable and able to manage your time and workload effectively.
To be eligible for our apprenticeship, you must:
• Have the full and unrestricted right to work in the UK.
• Have lived permanently in the UK for the last 3 years.
• Have achieved a grade C/4 in GCSE English and Maths.
• Not already hold a qualification that significantly overlaps with the content of this apprenticeship.

Our application process is designed to help you show your potential, not to test what you already know!
• Online application form – no CV required: We believe you're more than just a document, so we won’t ask you to submit a CV. Please upload a blank document on the application form.

At Howden, people are at the heart of everything we do. As an employee-owned business, we believe success is built through collaboration, learning and supporting one another. Ready to apply?

Job Description:
The Warranty Claims Manager will take end-to-end commercial ownership of supplier warranty issues across Europe, ensuring that defects are resolved efficiently, fairly and in line with Fluence’s contractual warranty rights. Sitting between the technical fix and the formal claim, the role will enforce supplier obligations before issues escalate—determining who is liable for parts and labour, pursuing recovery, and agreeing pragmatic commercial solutions where suppliers struggle to meet their warranty obligations. The role is central to protecting margin, holding suppliers accountable, and positioning Fluence as an organised, priority customer.
Key Responsibilities
•
Review and analyse Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs) relating to supplier-provided equipment, and assess the commercial and contractual impact on the affected project.
•
Determine warranty entitlement—confirming whether an issue is covered, and who bears responsibility for parts, labour and associated costs (supplier vs. Fluence).
•
Collaborate with the Quality team on root-cause and 8D analysis to establish the responsible party and capture supporting evidence.
•
Manage and execute the supplier warranty claims process end to end, including notification, documentation, RFIs, follow-up and challenge of supplier rejections.
•
Negotiate and agree commercial solutions where suppliers cannot meet warranty KPIs—for example credit notes, supplier-funded labour, replacement parts, warranty extensions or settlement packages.
•
Act as the single regional point of contact for suppliers on warranty matters, making it straightforward for suppliers to engage and resolve issues quickly.
•
Track and report recovery status, case ageing, credit notes and supplier response times, maintaining accurate records of claims, correspondence and outcomes.
•
Identify patterns and serial defects early, feeding failure data and lessons learned back to Engineering, Quality and Procurement to reduce recurrence.
•
Escalate only material, disputed or strategic matters to the Claims, Legal or Procurement/GPO teams, keeping routine warranty issues out of formal claims.
•
Drive continuous improvement of the warranty process to enhance accountability, recovery rates and supplier performance across the region.
Key Qualifications & Experience
•
Minimum 5+ years’ experience in warranty claims, supplier quality, contract or commercial management, ideally within the construction, energy or industrial manufacturing sectors.
•
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Quality Management, Law, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
•
Strong understanding of supplier warranty agreements and quality-assurance principles, with sound contractual and commercial acumen.
•
Demonstrated experience of NCR processes and root-cause analysis methodologies (e.g. 8D, Six Sigma / Lean).
•
Excellent analytical, communication and negotiation skills, with the ability to hold suppliers to account while maintaining constructive relationships.
•
Able to work independently, manage multiple stakeholders, and coordinate across Quality, Services, Procurement, Project Management, Finance and Legal.
•
Proficient in Microsoft Office and ERP/QMS systems (e.g. SAP, Oracle, or equivalent).
•
Actively contributes to the adoption of AI and digital innovation to support the transformation and future evolution of warranty and claims management (e.g. data analytics, defect-trend detection and process automation).
•
Familiarity with ISO 9001 or similar quality-management systems is desirable.
•
Six Sigma or Lean certification is a plus.
•
English business fluency
